ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows a common-emitter transistor amplifier circuit. The collector is connected to +VCC=+12 V through RC, and the emitter is grounded; the input signal is coupled to the base through C1, and the base is biased by RB; the output is connected from the collector node through the coupling capacitor C2 to the right-side load RL, and the lower end of RL is grounded. Therefore, C2 indicates that RL only participates in the AC load, and during DC quiescent bias, RL is blocked from DC and is not included in the DC collector loop. Then reason: At DC, the quiescent collector current is determined only by RC, ICQ=(VCC-UCEQ)/RC=(12 V-6 V)/3 kΩ=2 mA. At AC, C2 can be regarded as a short circuit, and the power-supply terminal is AC ground, so the collector AC load is RC in parallel with RL: Rac=RC||RL=3 kΩ||3 kΩ=1.5 kΩ. The output voltage swing allowed in the cutoff direction is ICQ·Rac=2 mA×1.5 kΩ=3 V; the allowed swing in the saturation direction is about UCEQ=6 V. To ensure no distortion, the smaller one should be taken, so the maximum undistorted output voltage is 3 V.
